summary: Mobile remote-control daemon exposes full-host file R/W and AI agent execution via hardcoded WebSocket
details: Package ships a CLI daemon (`agenthub-agent`) that opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded first-party endpoint `wss://agenthub-agent.fyenet.com` and dispatches inbound message envelopes to handlers that perform arbitrary filesystem read/write across the installer's drives (`FileRead`/`FileWrite`/`FileTree`/`FileSearch` via a `normalizePath` helper with no root sandbox) and drive a Claude Code SDK session on the host with `bypassPermissions` as the default mode, granting the paired remote party tool-execution capability on the machine. An `AgentUpdate` action received over the same WebSocket spawns `agenthub-agent update`, which runs `npm install` for a new version of the package and restarts the daemon, giving the server operator a remote channel to swap in any future published version. The `install` subcommand additionally writes autostart entries (Windows HKCU Run key, `~/.config/systemd/user/agenthub-agent.service`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agenthub.agenthub-agent.plist`) so the daemon reconnects on every login. The remote-control capability is the documented purpose of the package and the WebSocket endpoint is on the publisher's own domain, so the trust model is 'do I trust the maintainer of agenthub-ai to have arbitrary FS and AI-tool access to my host whenever the daemon is running and paired'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
